summary: Defines a :copy keyword parameter for the Sieve mail filtering language, letting fileinto and redirect actions deliver a copy without cancelling the default save to the inbox. Users get filing or forwarding without losing the original.

plainLanguage.summary: The Sieve :copy parameter lets fileinto or redirect send an extra copy while preserving the default inbox delivery. The RFC warns that the feature also makes covert copying easier.

subtitle: A Sieve :copy parameter for filing or redirecting a copy without changing normal delivery.

tldr.problem: Sieve fileinto and redirect actions cancel the default inbox save, so an extra copy can change how later script actions work.
tldr.mechanism: The optional :copy parameter makes fileinto or redirect act on a copy while leaving the implicit keep in place.
tldr.outcome: Scripts can copy a message without changing other handling, but the feature can make unnoticed eavesdropping easier.

today: RFC 3894 is a Proposed Standard. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Why Explicit Keep Can Cause Problems
sections.content:
Sieve controls the handling of incoming email. By default, a message is saved in the owner's inbox, but fileinto and redirect cancel that default behavior.

An explicit keep can preserve a message, but a later discard cannot undo that explicit keep. Scripts that try to track the implicit behavior can become unwieldy.
sections.plainLanguage: Filing or forwarding a message normally replaces inbox delivery. Adding an explicit keep can interfere with later rules, so the extension provides a direct copy action.

sections.title: The :copy Parameter
sections.content:
The extension adds optional :copy to fileinto and redirect. With the parameter, the action does not cancel the implicit keep; it files or redirects a copy as well as whatever else happens to the message.

The capability name and keyword are copy. A script must require the capability before using the parameter.
sections.plainLanguage: Adding :copy tells Sieve to file or forward a duplicate while leaving the default inbox handling active.

sections.title: Protecting Scripts and Mail Privacy
sections.content:
The extension makes it easier to eavesdrop on a user's message stream without the user noticing. Before this extension, an attacker with read/write access to Sieve scripts could do this; now the attacker does not need to parse a script to modify it.

The RFC says write access to Sieve scripts must be protected as strongly as read/write access to email. Organizations that monitor mail should consider local data-protection laws and set privacy expectations correctly.
sections.plainLanguage: Someone who can change a Sieve script can add hidden copies of messages. Protect script access as carefully as access to email.
